intro: Use short everyday texts to find a time, a price, a place or a simple instruction.
b1.texto: A short notice often gives one main piece of information: a time, place, price or rule. Read the heading and numbers first, then check the words around them. You do not need to understand every word to find a departure time or choose an item from a menu.
b3.f0: Open Monday to Saturday, 9:00 to 18:00. Closed on Sundays.
b4.f0: Set menu: soup, Spanish omelette or salad. Water included. Price: 12 euros.
b5.f0: Hi, I arrive at six. I will wait for you in front of the museum.
b7.pregunta: Which platform does the train to Toledo leave from?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Platform 3 is the platform the notice gives for the Toledo train.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Platform 10 is a different platform; the notice gives platform 3 for Toledo.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The notice does give a platform, so saying it does not say is wrong.
b8.o0.refuerzo: Lunes a sábado gives the days; the café opens these days from 9:00 to 18:00.
b8.o1.refuerzo: Every day would include Sunday, which does not match the days the café is open.
b8.o2.refuerzo: Only Sundays is the opposite of the answer; the café is open Monday to Saturday.
b9.pregunta: What is included in the set menu?
b9.o0.refuerzo: Water is the drink included in the set menu, so it is the right answer.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Coffee is not the item listed; the set menu includes water.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Dessert is not included; the set menu includes water instead.
